re_line: Kim inspects factories as Trump-Kim meeting fails · Democrats target Supreme Court chief · Yongbyon enrichment expansion confirmed · KOSPI drops 5.2%
morning_memo: Kim Jong Un inspected educational factory sites Saturday as KCNA ignored Trump's failed Asia-trip outreach.
Democratic Party set December 3 as target date to introduce Supreme Court Chief Justice Cho Hee-dae impeachment motion.
WSJ and multiple wire services reported new satellite imagery confirming expansion of Yongbyon uranium-enrichment facility.

imagery_report.label: Yongbyon uranium-enrichment facility expansion confirmed
imagery_report.headline: IAEA says North Korea has completed external construction on an enrichment facility extension at Yongbyon; WSJ publishes new satellite photos.
imagery_report.body: The International Atomic Energy Agency said North Korea has completed external works on an extension to its uranium-enrichment plant at Yongbyon, with the UN nuclear watchdog voicing serious concern over the upgrades. WSJ published new satellite photographs showing the expansion. The findings align with the BP Locations tracker noting the enrichment building expansion was complete and a new centrifuge hall operational as of April 2026, with thermal signatures consistent with increased production.

bp_locations.name: Yongbyon Nuclear Complex
bp_locations.note: As of April 2026: Enrichment building expansion complete, new centrifuge hall operational. 5 MWe reactor and IRT-2000 both running. Thermal signatures consistent with increased plutonium/HEU production.

bp_locations.name: Sinpo South Shipyard
bp_locations.note: As of May 2025: Hero Kim Kun Ok SLBM submarine exited drydock after more than two years of fitting-out but was still not operational. New submarine construction begun in separate bay. NK Pro satellite analysis (Oct 20 2026) separately reports North Korea's Nampho Shipyard missed a deadline earlier in Oct 2026 to launch a 5,000-ton naval destroyer, with hull sections visible at two potential outdoor assembly areas. 38 North analysis published Oct 30 documents public display of a vessel described as a 'Tactical Nuclear Attack' submarine. Kim Jong Un inspected Nampho Shipyard on Nov 7 (reported Nov 8 by KCNA), announcing a new warship under construction larger than the destroyer built last year. NK News reported on Nov 6 that North Korea has expanded warship construction to a third shipyard. 38 North published analysis on Nov 11 of the Choe Hyon destroyer and its strategic implications for the West Sea Fleet. NK News identified a second major east-coast naval base project on Nov 13, beyond the Munchon-area site Kim inspected on Nov 12.

bp_locations.name: THAAD Site, Seongju County
bp_locations.note: As of March 2026: All 6 THAAD launchers were redeployed to the Middle East amid Iran tensions. At least 2 launchers may have returned to Seongju by late March 2026. Battery operational status remains uncertain. This report is from March 2026 and may not reflect the current state.

bp_locations.name: Sohae Satellite Launch Station
bp_locations.note: As of March 2026: 2,500 kN engine test stand firing observed. Two villages razed for facility expansion. New seaport and large assembly building nearing completion. This report is from March 2026 and may not reflect the current state.

bp_locations.name: Punggye-ri Nuclear Test Site
bp_locations.note: As of November 2025: ROK Defense Intelligence Agency assessed Tunnel No. 3 is test-ready and a nuclear test can be conducted at any time upon political decision. Site maintained at high readiness since mid-2024. This report is from November 2025 and may not reflect the current state.

bp_locations.name: Tumangang–Khasan (NK-Russia border)
bp_locations.note: As of March 2026: Road bridge construction accelerated, completion target moved to Summer 2026. Passenger rail service resumed mid-2025. Ore and tank car traffic at highest levels since project began. This report is from March 2026 and may not reflect the current state. Russian Transport Ministry applications filed November 13, 2026 for a 14-daily-round-trip Vladivostok-Rason bus route over the new vehicle bridge, with experts noting the service will likely transport DPRK workers more than Russian tourists.

bp_locations.name: Sinuiju–Dandong (NK-China border)
bp_locations.note: NK News Planet Labs satellite imagery analyzed through November 15, 2026 confirms trucks filling Sinuiju customs facility from October 16, the day after the New Yalu River Bridge officially opened, with activity peaking October 19–20. A wall of 40-foot containers bearing Maersk and COSCO markings was visible on the Chinese side. Kim Jong Un crossed the New Yalu River Bridge on October 24 during his unannounced visit to Dandong. Daily NK reported November 12 that Chinese truck drivers who relied on side income ferrying parcels across the new bridge are souring on operations due to tighter customs checks and movement controls. Huanghai Automobile's Dandong bus factory announced November 13 it is operating at full capacity following Kim Jong Un's October visit. Daily NK reported November 18 that Sinuiju markets are overflowing with Chinese goods but a severe cash shortage means almost nobody is buying, with vendors describing a 'trading cliff.'

bp_locations.name: Rason SEZ
bp_locations.note: As of November 2025: Chinese businesspeople re-entry to Rason SEZ expanded. Coal exports through Rason at highest levels in years throughout 2025. Arms export berth also active. This report is from November 2025 and may not reflect the current state.

bp_locations.name: Yellow Sea NLL
bp_locations.note: As of September 26, 2025: 140m DPRK merchant vessel Toksong crossed the Northern Limit Line near Baengnyeong Island, advanced 5km south. ROK Navy fired approximately 60 warning shots; vessel retreated after 1 hour. ROK Marine Corps Commandant Gen. Ju Il-suk stated October 20, 2026 that North Korea has made 'various changes' to forces facing South Korea's border islands, with Seoul stepping up surveillance along the maritime border. 38 North satellite imagery published October 29 shows North Korea continuing to install new fencing along its border. North Korean propaganda loudspeakers were visible at two border locations on November 4, 2026 from Odusan Unification Observatory and Key Observatory in Gyeonggi Province. ROK Joint Chiefs confirmed November 6, 2026 that a drifting North Korean fishing vessel was spotted in international waters off Ulleung Island on November 3 and is under investigation.

bp_locations.name: Yellow Sea PMZ
bp_locations.note: As of January 27-28, 2026: Atlantic Amsterdam (converted oil rig, Chinese aquaculture platform) relocated out of the Provisional Measures Zone to Weihai shipyard following President Lee Jae-myung's Beijing state visit. Two giant aquaculture cages (Shen Lan 1, Shen Lan 2) and 13 buoys remain in the PMZ. This report is from January 2026 and may not reflect the current state.

bp_locations.name: Vostochny/Dunai
bp_locations.note: As of January 2026: Arms shipments slowed due to ice, one Russian vessel (likely Angara or Lady R) visited Rason, docked January 14, 2026 at arms export berth. Cargo routed to Vostochny. Since September 2023: 64 voyages by 4 vessels (Angara, Maria, Maya-1, Lady R) delivered approximately 15,800 containers (approximately 4.2-5.8 million munitions) from Rajin to Vostochny/Dunai. This report is from January 2026 and may not reflect the current state. Russian Transport Ministry applications filed November 13, 2026 for a Vladivostok-Rason bus route operating 14 daily round trips.

rok_government.action: Lee sets minimum 100 million won reward per case for CSAT cheating reports
rok_government.detail: President Lee clarified on social media that the government reward for reporting College Scholastic Ability Test cheating is at least 100 million won per case, not a maximum, and that multiple reports multiply the reward. Lee called exam cheating "a crime as serious as corruption by public officials."

rok_government.action: Chung meets US Ambassador Steel and USFK Commander Brunson at Panmunjom
rok_government.detail: Unification Minister **Chung Dong-young** held a rare meeting with US Ambassador Steel and United States Forces Korea (USFK) Commander Gen. **Xavier Brunson** at Panmunjom, the first encounter with the ambassador after a 113-day delay. The venue and format were described by Korean media as unusual.

top_stories.headline: New satellite photos confirm expansion of North Korea's Yongbyon uranium-enrichment plant
top_stories.body: The Wall Street Journal published new satellite photographs showing expansion of the uranium-enrichment facility at Yongbyon, the same day the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) said North Korea has completed external works on an enrichment facility extension and voiced serious concern over the upgrades. The IAEA finding, corroborated by Reuters, AP, and France 24, aligns with the BP Locations tracker showing a new centrifuge hall operational since April 2026 with thermal signatures consistent with increased production.

top_stories.headline: Democratic Party targets December 3 for Supreme Court chief justice impeachment motion
top_stories.body: The Democratic Party of Korea formally adopted the impeachment of Supreme Court Chief Justice **Cho Hee-dae** as party policy on November 20, naming Rep. Yang Bu-nam to lead a task force, and SBS reported the party has set December 3, the second anniversary of the martial law declaration, as the target date to introduce the motion. With 161 seats, the party can pass the motion without opposition support; the constitution requires introduction by at least 100 members and passage by 150. The People Power Party announced it would defend Cho and held a rally in Daegu that the party claimed drew 100,000 participants.

top_stories.headline: Kim inspects educational factory sites as KCNA ignores Trump's Asia trip outreach
top_stories.body: North Korean state media released images Saturday showing **Kim Jong Un** examining teaching aids and science class equipment at factory sites, with KCNA saying he inspected samples of school fixtures "of all indices." Trump departed Asia after the APEC summit in Shenzhen without meeting Kim, saying the encounter did not "work out" but that the meeting would happen "at some point"; Pyongyang has not commented on Trump's remarks. Trump told reporters that the US-China-Russia trilateral at APEC discussed Korean Peninsula dangers.

also_today.headline: Lee visits Ulsan SK AI data center, pledges support for regional mega-projects
also_today.body_text: President Lee said AI data centers are "a major source of demand for semiconductors" and called for speed in the global AI race, warning that construction-worker shortages for advanced facilities require government attention. The Ulsan visit follows a visit to Samsung's Asan campus two weeks earlier, completing a tour of the three regional mega-project zones.

also_today.headline: KEIA: Kim Jong Un's China visit warrants greater scrutiny
also_today.body_text: The Korea Economic Institute of America published analysis arguing Kim Jong Un's October visit to China deserves closer examination given its implications for DPRK-China-Russia alignment. The piece appeared as Trump's Asia trip ended without a Kim meeting and expert analysts told the Korea Herald that DPRK-US talks are unlikely.

The Section 122 surcharge expired July 24, so there is no baseline reciprocal tariff currently in force. Section 301 is now the primary prospective vehicle for new tariff measures on South Korea.

business_economy.headline: Korea's China trade surplus of $43.3B hides widening non-semiconductor deficit
business_economy.body_text: Korea's trade balance with China turned to a *$43.3 billion* surplus in January–October 2026, the first surplus in four years, driven entirely by semiconductor exports of $124.3 billion. Excluding semiconductors, the deficit with China widened by $12.4 billion year-on-year, with autos, batteries, and electric equipment all deteriorating.

business_economy.headline: Nasdaq plunges 5.3% as tech selloff erases 2026 annual gains; KOSPI fell 5.2% on Nov 20
business_economy.body_text: The Nasdaq composite fell *5.28 percent* on November 20, erasing all 2026 gains, as semiconductor stocks including Nvidia (-14%), SK Hynix (-13.1%), and AMD (-13.25%) collapsed. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index fell 10.73 percent; the VIX spiked to 35.89, the highest since April 2025.

business_economy.headline: Korean retail investors bought 800 billion won of Nvidia after Jensen Huang scandal; now sitting on 6 trillion won loss
business_economy.body_text: Korean retail investors net-bought *612 million dollars* ($817 billion won) of Nvidia shares from October 30 to November 19, following the Jensen Huang scandal-driven price drop, but their total Nvidia holdings fell 26.5 percent in value over the same period to a 6.1 trillion won unrealized loss.

business_economy.headline: Korea Zinc fires back at MBK-Youngpoong offensive over Homeplus and accounting violations
business_economy.body_text: Korea Zinc rejected pressure from its activist shareholders MBK Partners and Youngpoong, demanding they first account for Homeplus's collapse and accounting rule violations before questioning Korea Zinc's governance. The escalating proxy battle continues ahead of a shareholder vote.

business_economy.headline: South Korea gasoline prices fall for 27th straight week; Seoul average enters 1,800-won range
business_economy.body_text: The national average gasoline price fell to 1,854.7 won per liter in the third week of November, the 27th consecutive weekly decline, with Seoul entering the 1,800-won range at 1,899.4 won. Dubai crude averaged $89.3 per barrel last week, down $0.40.

northeast_asia.headline: Japanese affinity for South Korea hits record 62%, while China sentiment remains low
northeast_asia.body_text: A Japanese government survey found 62 percent of Japanese respondents feel friendly toward South Korea, the highest level on record, as Japan-Korea ties have warmed. Affinity toward China remained at a low level reflecting deteriorating Japan-China relations.

northeast_asia.headline: Switzerland sanctions North Korea's Songdowon youth camp for role in Ukraine child transfers
northeast_asia.body_text: Switzerland added North Korea's Songdowon International Youth Camp to its Russia-related sanctions list, following UK and EU designations, citing participation in transfers of Ukrainian children. The trilateral designations expand the multilateral sanctions perimeter around DPRK entities involved in Russia's Ukraine operations.

rok_assembly.action: National Assembly passes Democracy Patriots Act
rok_assembly.detail: The National Assembly passed legislation providing state honors and benefits to victims and contributors to South Korea's democratization movement, over People Power Party opposition.

calendar_watch.headline: Mongolia FM Battsetseg begins four-day official visit to Seoul
calendar_watch.detail: Mongolian Foreign Minister Battsetseg is scheduled to make an official visit to South Korea from November 22 to 25, according to Korean media reports.

calendar_watch.headline: Justice minister nominee Lee Yong-cheol confirmation hearing
calendar_watch.detail: Justice Minister nominee Lee Yong-cheol faces a National Assembly confirmation hearing on November 24, with opposition lawmakers signaling scrutiny over allegations of attorney registration law violations.

calendar_watch.headline: Democrats target Dec. 3 for Supreme Court chief justice impeachment motion
calendar_watch.detail: The Democratic Party has set December 3, the second anniversary of the martial law declaration, as the target date to formally introduce the impeachment motion against Chief Justice Cho Hee-dae in the National Assembly.

opeds_today.headline: Experts React: Takeaways from President Trump's Trip to Asia
opeds_today.central_argument: Trump's Asia trip produced symbolic wins, including Xi's airport greeting, but yielded few tangible outcomes, with the Trump-Xi-Putin trilateral at APEC ignoring that only global victors can hold a 'Yalta,' and trade issues punted to the December G20 in Miami.
opeds_today.summary: CSIS experts assess Trump's Manila and Shenzhen stops across the ASEAN, Quad, and APEC summits. The analysis notes Xi's unprecedented airport greeting undercut arguments that Beijing has the upper hand, while the trilateral with Putin was more pageant than substance. For Korea policy, the absence of a Trump-Kim meeting and the North Korea nuclear discussion at the trilateral are the primary takeaways.

opeds_today.headline: Between a Rock and a Hard Place: Evaluating the Risks of Chinese Memory Chips
opeds_today.central_argument: With SK Hynix sold out of DRAM and HBM through 2029 and the United States facing a deepening memory chip shortage, US policymakers face a genuine dilemma between accepting Chinese DRAM to fill supply gaps and the security risks of dependence on Chinese memory producers.
opeds_today.summary: CSIS examines the acute US DRAM shortage driven by HBM demand consuming up to 70 percent of capacity at Micron, SK Hynix, and Samsung, with no relief expected before 2030. The analysis directly bears on Korean chipmakers' strategic position and the US-Korea semiconductor relationship, as Washington weighs allowing Chinese suppliers to fill gaps in consumer and defense applications.

kcna_delta.kim_activity: Kim Jong Un inspected educational factory sites, examining samples of school fixtures and science class equipment.

top_articles.headline: North Korean media focuses on allies during APEC summit week, ignoring Trump's meeting overture
top_articles.summary: NK News reported that North Korean state media focused on DPRK diplomatic ties with allied states during the week of the Shenzhen APEC summit, with no KCNA output acknowledging Trump's remarks about wanting to meet Kim.

kcna_delta.bottom_line: State media released Kim's educational factory inspection as the dominant domestic image of the day, maintaining silence on Trump's failed outreach and the Shenzhen APEC trilateral discussion of Korean Peninsula dangers.

capitol_hill.headline: 2026 midterms deliver new alliance defenders in Congress; Democrats take both chambers
capitol_hill.body_text: KEIA analysis argues Seoul should engage the new Congress before positions harden, drawing on the 2018 midterm precedent when Democrats capped USFK troop levels at 28,500.

korea_world.headline: South Korea's defense industry expands Middle East push beyond arms exports to production and technology cooperation
korea_world.body_text: South Korea's defense industry is deepening its Middle East engagement by moving beyond equipment sales to production and technology cooperation arrangements, accelerating a broader shift in global defense competition dynamics. The move reflects Seoul's strategic effort to diversify defense partnerships.

korea_world.headline: South Korea eyes two Thai rail lines and Bangkok Port revamp
korea_world.body_text: South Korea is pursuing contracts for two Thai railway lines and a Bangkok Port revamp, as Seoul expands infrastructure export partnerships in Southeast Asia. No contract value or timeline was reported.
